states.name: narrow
states.gap: Line pitch is 74 device / 37 logical px against A's 76 / 38 — leading of 1.68 vs 1.73 on identical 22-logical-px type, so the block sets ~3% denser and the same first paragraph costs 7 lines instead of 6; the page packs where A breathes, and its last body line clears the status-bar rule by 19 device px against A's 35.
states.gapTheirs: The column is poured to fill the window: side margins of only 140 device / 70 logical px (7.3% of the 960-logical width) around a 63-character, ~812-logical-px measure, against B's 179 device / 90 logical px margins and 58-character, ~771-px measure — an 8% wider set inside a 22% thinner frame. Worse, the reading edge is not one edge: body words start at x=142 device, the # heading's words at 193, the ## heading's words at 218, so the prose jogs 26 and 38 logical px inward at every heading, while B keeps every word — heading or body — on 181–184.
states.verdict: Two calm grey pages, and only one of them was actually measured. A's tell is the left edge: the body sits on 142, the # heading's words on 193, the ## heading's words on 218, so the column you read down wobbles by up to 38 logical px every time a heading arrives, and it does that inside 70-px margins that leave the text looking poured into the window rather than set on a page. B buys its narrower 58-character measure and 90-px margins at the price of a ragged ink edge — ## at 102, # at 128, body at 181 — and 1 logical px less leading, which is the only thing A wins and is under the threshold you would feel at arm's length. Paper is a wash: #f9f9f9 against #f7f7f7, two levels of grey nobody has ever noticed while writing.

states.name: short
states.gap: Tighter leading: baseline pitch 74px against A's 76px, on type that is ~1.3% larger (identical 61-char line spans 1628px in B vs 1607px in A) — line-height ≈1.66 vs ≈1.73, about 4% less air per line, ~10px less over the six-line block.
states.gapTheirs: The heading's words break the page's left rule: body lines start at x=623 but 'The Note on the Table' starts at x=675 — a 53px (2 monospace cells) step right, with only a small marker glyph left holding the margin. B sets heading text flush at x=623 with every paragraph line, so the column has one unbroken left edge; A's most prominent line reads as an accidental indent, and at ## / ### that inset becomes a 4- and 6-cell staircase down the left side.
states.verdict: These are the same page within a couple of percent — same ~62-character measure, same ~1636px column optically centred (622/626 vs 623/621), same flat near-grey paper two levels apart, same 6px caret filling the line box, same two-pitch paragraph gap — so the decision comes down to one edge and one pitch. A gives you 2px more leading per line and then squanders it by shoving the title 53px inside the paragraph edge, which is the one misalignment you cannot stop seeing once you have seen it, and it compounds with every heading level. B holds a single straight spine at x=623 for title and prose alike and pays for it with 74px pitch, which at this size is still comfortable, if a touch dense. Neither page is doing anything brave: both are a grey rectangle in a grey field, and A's is the one with the burr in it.
